description:
lib.rs:76:
    pub fn register_metadata_handlers<B>(dispatcher: &mut Dispatcher<B::CallerCtx>, backend: Arc<B>) where ...

What callers cannot depend on:
- What happens if a caller calls register_metadata_handlers twice on the same dispatcher with two different backends? Does the second call replace the first, panic, no-op, or accumulate handlers? The doc says 'After this call the dispatcher handles: Metadata/get, Metadata/changes, ...' but is silent on prior registrations for those names.
- The behavior depends on jmap_server::Dispatcher::register, which is not part of jmap_metadata_server's documented contract. A future Dispatcher behavior change (e.g. from 'last write wins' to 'panic on duplicate') is silently a behavior change here.
- The doc does not say whether register_metadata_handlers is safe to call from multiple threads concurrently. The dispatcher takes &mut, so the borrow checker forbids it, but a sophisticated caller using interior-mutable dispatcher wrappers cannot tell from the docs whether the function itself is thread-safe.
- The doc does not say whether the backend Arc must be the same one passed to every related crate. In a real consumer that registers Mail + Metadata + Chat handlers on one dispatcher, the question 'must I use the same Arc instance?' is answered (no — Arc::clone semantics) but the doc says 'Pass the same Arc<B> to both this function and any application-level code that needs the backend directly' which strongly implies a single Arc identity matters when it does not.

Recommendation:
- Add a paragraph: 'Calling register_metadata_handlers more than once on the same Dispatcher overwrites prior handlers for the five method names. Concurrent calls are not supported (the &mut Dispatcher argument enforces this at the type system level).'
- Reword the 'Pass the same Arc<B>' line to 'You may pass any Arc<B> — the function clones it internally. Sharing the same Arc<B> across all your registrations is a memory optimization, not a correctness requirement.'

What goes wrong if this stays:
- A consumer wiring multiple capability families onto one Dispatcher cannot predict whether 'register everything, then mutate one' will work, will silently shadow, or will need a deregister-first dance. They will write defensive code that the contract does not require.
title: API: register_metadata_handlers idempotency / overwrite contract unspecified
